🧵 my imaginative broad strokes on new storyworlds

(I’m basically gonna drop each word into my gut and riff on whatever comes up—let’s give it a go) https://t.co/aDLnSUbjB6
  [Quoting Tweet 1468143075184758784 (missing)]
↓
1468156114470637574 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 6
ORTHOTOPIA: “right/correct/upright place”
Fairly boring 1950s america vibes. You keep expecting things to take a turn for the Stepford, but they never actually do. Everyone grins, pats their kids on the back, and whistles Andy Griffith theme.
↓
1468156116941119493 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5 🔁 1
The stories here are tragedies—people who see problems, conformity, straight jackets of uprightness. They want change and push for it, but are always either defeated or subsumed into the system they hate, slowly co-opted without realizing it.
↓
1468159700776759296 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 6
SOPHOTOPIA: “wise place”

Very idyllic place, mostly relaxed. Not exactly high tech or low tech—the tech that enriches individuals and communities stays around, while the tech that causes disharmony or degradation is left to rot.
↓
1468159702517399555 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5
There are fewer people than you’d expect, for a variety of reasons. The stories here mostly revolve around big adventures young people take, into nature, from community to community, into the Otherworld—we watch wisdom form through rough contact w self and world.
↓
1468159704044126211 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5
Actually, stories could be any hard transition. Middle age to old age. Husband to widower. A disaster hitting the community. 

Any chance to see that wisdom here doesn’t mean having all the right answers, or some soft-eyes complacent confidence;;
↓
1468160155653218308 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5
It means engaging fully with who & where you are, your points of contact with the world around you, the points of contact in the world outside you.

Sometimes wisdom works out well. Sometimes it ends in tears. Sometimes it’s a trickster God’s weird joke. But it’s worthwhile.
↓
1468162219342970881 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 4
ANOTOPIA: “upward place.”

I’m getting nothing on this one. People moving into the mountains to avoid a lowland catastrophe? Idk. Human society only existing above the pollution. Journeys into the poisoned places, revealing hidden secrets.
↓
1468165091946385408 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 7
HYPERTOPIA: “Super-Place” “the placiest place of all”

This one would take a lot more thinking to flesh out into anything workable, but I’m seeing a world where place is the most kmportant thing.
↓
1468165093431070728 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5
People are quite porous, affected by the spaces they’ve been, they are, they were raised in. 

Near animistic sense of different land, buildings, spaces having their own personalities and qualities that sink into the people who spend time there.
↓
1468165094911655937 [2021-12-07] @the_wilderless 💜 5
Tons of good directions to take here, but the basic idea is the most exciting thing for me rn.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a scattered collection of aspirational tweets about storytelling and self-authorship, spanning 2010-2025. While there is a recurring thematic boundary object—'write your own story'—there is no discernible evolutionary arc, dialectical engagement, or knowledge production. The tweets are largely motivational aphorisms (tasshinfogleman's resilience thread, julianweisser's 'future as fiction') interspersed with creative writing exercises (blisstweeting's micro-stories, the_wilderless's worldbuilding). The 2019 exchange between sharanvkaur and visakanv about South Asian women's narrative ownership is the only moment of substantive discourse, but it remains isolated. This is a 'vibes-only' strand—thematically coherent but structurally inert.

essential_tweets.annotation: The sole substantive moment: sharanvkaur surfaces an essay on South Asian women's narrative erasure, introducing the only conflict/depth in the strand.
The core tension articulated: 'This story is not ours. If we exist, it's as helpers.'—a rare instance of structural critique rather than platitude.
visakanv's response ('your story is yours to tell') exemplifies the strand's typical mode: supportive but not generative.
the_wilderless's worldbuilding thread is the most creative artifact, but it's a solo riff with no community uptake or iteration.
blisstweeting's writing prompt thread: a burst of craft practice, but again no collaborative evolution or lasting framework.
tasshinfogleman's 'tell a good story' becomes the most-repeated refrain, but it remains a mantra rather than a method.
The Stoic framing ('focus on what is in my control') is the closest to actionable philosophy, but it's generic self-help.
mimi10v3's 'twitter as self-authorship' captures the strand's central aspiration but offers no toolkit for execution.
julianweisser's 'future starts as fiction' is the most memeable distillation, but it's a restatement, not a refinement.
michaelgarfield's 2010 'Stories :)' is included for chronological bookending—the earliest signal of the theme, though contextless.
